chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from someone else who was present with him, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), so I said, 'O maid, give me a drink of water.' So he (peace be upon him) said to her: 'Give him a drink of my Nabeez.' So she came to me with Nabeez made from partially-ripened dates (Busr) in a brass cup. He said, so I said, 'The people of Kufa are not satisfied with this.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So what is their Nabeez?' I said to him (peace be upon him), 'They put Al-Qa'wa in it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is Al-Qa'wa?' I said, 'Al-Daazy.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is Al-Daazy?' So I said, 'Pressed dates.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The vessel is stained by it until the Nabeez ferments, then it boils, then it intoxicates, so it is drunk.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is Prohibited.'

key_terms.الدَّاذِيّ: Al-Daazy: A specific type of pressed dates or date residue.
key_terms.الْقَعْوَة: Al-Qa'wa: A term referring to the residue or pressed dates used to flavor or ferment the drink.
key_terms.بُسْر: Busr: Partially ripe dates, often used for Nabeez.
key_terms.ثُفْل: Thufl: Pressed or squeezed dates (residue after extracting juice).
key_terms.نَبِيذ: Nabeez: A drink made by soaking dates or raisins in water.

ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the juristic distinction between permissible Nabeez and that which becomes intoxicating through specific preparation methods. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies the Kufan practice of using 'Al-Daazy' (pressed date pulp) to coat the vessel, which accelerates fermentation until it causes intoxication, as the key factor rendering it Haram. This underscores the Shia principle that the prohibition of Nabeez is contingent upon its potential to intoxicate, rather than the mere presence of dates.
